attempts.summary: Implemented Ansible-driven filesystem snapshot/restore for /srv/data on node1, controlled from node2 (the only node with Ansible installed). Since node1 (RHEL7) is on plain partitions with no free space (no LVM/btrfs) and has only Python 2.7 (incompatible with Ansible core 2.20's Python-3-only module code), the playbook uses `raw` SSH-command tasks and implements snapshots as timestamped tar.gz archives of /srv/data under /srv/snapshots. Executed the full cycle: seeded /srv/data, took a baseline snapshot, modified the directory (edited a file, deleted one, added two extraneous ones), then ran the Ansible restore play, which wiped /srv/data and extracted the snapshot — verified via sha256sum that content was restored byte-for-byte to the pre-modification baseline. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both node1 and node2: captured boot_id baselines, rebooted each node individually, confirmed boot_id changed on each, and verified post-restart recovery (data checksums intact and snapshot files present on node1; Ansible tooling and SSH control path intact on node2, followed by a live re-run of the snapshot play against node1 to prove the control path fully recovered).
